messages:
jess (runtime): Heads up — after the NF4/FP4 kernel handoff last night we’re seeing a sustained throughput drop (~18%) on p82 canaries and a memory spike on two pods :chart_with_downwards_trend: 

omar (perf): I see the same in telemetry. Prefix cache hit rate fell from 92% -> 76% around 03:12 UTC. KV memory RSS jumped ~1.2GB on the affected workers.

li (eng-runtime): timeline? which commit flipped the kernel?

jess (runtime): deploy-bot rolled kernel v3.7.1 -> v3.8.0 at 03:10 UTC (canary only). deploy-bot: deployment https://deploys.internal/r/7890

maria (ml): quick note — calibration table changed in the model artifact (nf4) earlier in the day. Could be quantization scale differences interacting with the new kernels.

omar (perf): uploaded perf profiles to the trace bucket: gs://perf-traces/1865467890/nf4-handoff.tar.gz. Top lines show heavy time in matmul kernel switch path and cache eviction loop. Snippet: 
```
# perf top -p <pid>
53.2%   kernel.so  [.] nf4_matmul_qk_kernel
12.0%   runtime.so [.] kv_cache_evict_batch
7.8%    runtime.so [.] batch_scheduler::flush_ready
```

li (eng-runtime): kv_cache_evict_batch spikes worry me — could be fragmentation when the kernel now packs KV differently. Any difference in per-chunk alignment?

jess (runtime): yes, kernel v3.8 switched to 128-byte packing for compressed KV pages (was 64). That reduces peak GPU memory but changes CPU scatter/gather patterns. Might be causing more frequent small evictions.

omar (perf): reproduced locally: with new kernel and same workload throughput drops when batch size > 16. If we limit batch_size to 8, throughput returns to baseline but latency variance increases.

li (eng-runtime): can we patch batching heuristic quickly? e.g., prefer smaller batches when KV eviction rate > threshold.

jess (runtime): I pushed a canary override to reduce max_continuous_batch to 12 for the affected pool. Monitoring now.

sre-bot: ALERT p82-canary pod-7: memory_rss increased by 1.1GB, kv_evictions/sec 42 -> 320, tail_latency_p95 320ms -> 860ms

maria (ml): if this is due to calibration changes, we should compare per-token quant scales. I can run a diff between artifacts 2026-03-15 vs 2026-03-16.

omar (perf): action items I suggest:
- revert kernel on canary to v3.7.1 (quick rollback)
- mitigate batching heuristic (short-term)
- deep profile on kernel packing path (long-term)

li (eng-runtime): I’ll open a rollback PR for canary and a positive gating for kernel swaps.

jess (runtime): +1 on rollback. Also tagging runtime-owners for postmortem: @omar, @li, @maria.

deploy-bot: rollback triggered for canary group at 03:46 UTC by li. Request: RB-4521.

sre-bot: INFO canary rollback completed at 03:47 UTC — metrics returning toward baseline.

omar (perf): after rollback, kv_evictions/sec back to 48, throughput recovered to ~98% baseline. Will continue extended profiling overnight and produce a short postmortem doc.

jess (runtime): thanks. For the postmortem please include: perf flamegraphs, KV fragmentation map, batching histograms, and the calibration diff that maria will provide.

maria (ml): will produce calibration diff. early hint: a handful of tensors had different symmetric vs asymmetric scale choices — could interact with packer.

li (eng-runtime): assigning follow-ups: RB-4521 (rollback done), TASK-983: heuristic limiter and eviction threshold; TASK-984: kernel packing compatibility test in integration harness.

jess (runtime): leaving this thread open until the postmortem PR lands. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
